text:
sre-oncall: FYI apiserver p95 in eu-west3 jumped to ~1s right when a large GPU onboarding batch hit. controller-manager flapped twice. anyone on it?
maria: noticed increased etcd timeouts and "dial tcp ...:2379: i/o timeout" in apiserver logs during the batch.
tony: checking NAT metrics now — SNAT port utilization spiked to 95% across 3 node pools. conntrack counts increased rapidly.
sre-oncall: logs: ```E0315 09:12:07 watch.go:45] watch 'pods' failed: dial tcp 10.20.5.3:2379: i/o timeout
controller-manager: error renewing lease: context deadline exceeded```
lee: looks like the provisioner burst opened a few hundred ephemeral connections to control plane + external registries. SNAT shortage leads to TCP resets which bubble into etcd RPCs.
infra-bot: Created ticket NET-2026-334 and alerted network-team. :loud_sound:
tony: briefly limited the provisioner concurrency from 80 -> 8 and paused remaining batches. watching metrics.
maria: after throttling, conntrack dropped and etcd rpc errors subsided. apiserver p95 back to ~160ms. controller-manager stable.
lee: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) add ephemeral port headroom in eu-west3 (extra NAT IPs) 2) make provisioner preflight check for SNAT/headroom 3) route heavy external pulls through a proxy to reuse connections 4) backpressure at the provisioner when conntrack > 400k
sre-oncall: agree. cost estimate for extra NAT IPs ~ $15k/mo — add to RFC for NAT capacity. also want a prewarm step to open persistent control-plane connections from new nodes to avoid huge burst.
deploy-bot: rollback: provisioner v2 -> v1 (triggered by maria)
tony: follow-up actions: I will add a soft cap in the provisioner and a metric-based semaphore. lee, can you draft the RFC for NAT capacity + prewarm?
lee: on it, will include cost/ops runbook and an emergency throttle.
sre-oncall: nice work. keeping INC open for 24h for observation. post-mortem if recurrence. :thumbsup:
